sources.entry: Squid - Caching proxy for the Web supporting HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, and more. It reduces bandwidth and improves response times by caching and reusing frequently-requested web pages. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 C/deb

summary.name: Squid
summary.one_liner: Squid is a caching proxy for the Web that supports HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and more, reducing bandwidth use and improving response times by caching and reusing frequently requested pages.
use_cases: Reduce bandwidth usage on an internet connection
Speed up web access for ISP users
Accelerate a website by caching content in front of web servers
Route and load balance requests across web servers
Distribute content to clients in multiple locations
summary.what_it_does: Squid is a caching proxy supporting HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and other protocols. It caches frequently requested web content and reuses it to save bandwidth and improve response times. It has extensive access controls and can act as a server accelerator. Squid can route content requests to servers in various ways to build cache hierarchies and content clusters. The page says it runs on most operating systems, including Windows, and is licensed under the GNU GPL.
notable: Server accelerator and reverse proxy use
Content routing to build cache hierarchies and load-balanced clusters
Used by many ISPs and websites; Wikimedia reports about 75% hit rate
caveats: Page says only that it runs on 'most available operating systems, including Windows'; macOS and Linux are not named on the page, so they are listed from general knowledge only and should be verified
